# Review round 5

Branch docs/issue-316-flow-prompt-audit. Findings below are copied verbatim from each reviewer subagent's final report: the section headings (which carry the severity) and every finding row or line that names tier-gate.sh, block-unchecked-merge.sh, block-destructive.sh, command-parse.sh, or their test files. Lines that do not name those files are omitted.

## Round-5 security review (c51e2877)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-a150fafe177ddf3c9.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-30T06:52:14.896Z

Every row below was run through the hooks themselves, at base (`git archive f3a39d72`) and at head (worktree, c51e2877), against a scratch repo with a bare origin and tags v1 and v2. Results are written `TG` (tier-gate), `BUM` (block-unchecked-merge) and `BD` (block-destructive); `.` means allowed with no output, `ask` is the confirmation prompt, `rc2` is a refusal. To confirm bash really runs each action, I ran the payloads under `/bin/bash` with `set -x`, a stub `gh` that prints its arguments, and `git push --dry-run`. Nothing was sent to GitHub.
The five suites I ran are green at head: block-destructive-git (142 passing), block-destructive-rm (65), block-destructive-branch (32), block-unchecked-merge (193) and e2e-guard-refusals (329). None of them contains a glued-substitution case. I did not run e2e-tier-gate or e2e-tier-gate-fences.
## Security Review Findings
### P1 — Critical Security Issues (Blocks Merge)
| **SEC-1 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:686`** (also `:675`, and the end-of-path matching at `tier-gate.sh:1153-1154`)<br>**Regression from 840f16ec.** The `__BD_SUBST__` marker is now glued to its word. So `.../merge$(true)` reads as `merge__BD_SUBST__`, and the endpoint patterns `*/pulls/*/merge`, `*/merges` and `*/releases` no longer match. The comment at `tier-gate.sh:1277` says "`/merge` would have to be written", and here it is written. Bash runs `gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/1/merge` (stub output confirmed).<br>`gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/1/merge$(true)`: TG base ask / head `.`; BUM base rc2 / head `.`<br>`` gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/1/merge`true` ``: same result<br>`gh api -X POST repos/o/r/merges$(true) -f base=main -f head=x`: TG ask → `.`; BUM rc2 → `.`<br>`gh api repos/o/r/releases$(true) -f tag_name=v9`: TG ask → `.`<br>`gh api -X POST repos/o/r/releases$(true) -f tag_name=v9`: TG ask → `.`<br>Same class, already allowed at base: `.../merge"$(true)"` and `gh api -X$(true) POST .../releases` are `.` at both, and BUM passes the first at both. _(HIGH)_ | When a word holds a glued marker, also judge it with the marker removed, since the substitution's output can be empty. Do this in TG's gh api endpoint and method reading and in BUM. Pin each row above in e2e-tier-gate and block-unchecked-merge. |
| **SEC-2 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:686`** (as read by `block-destructive.sh` and `block-unchecked-merge.sh` through `_bd_words`)<br>**Regression from the same change.** Destructive and merge commands that base refused are now allowed. `--hard$(true)` is `--hard` to bash; `set -x` showed `git reset --hard HEAD` and `git checkout .` running.<br>BD base rc2 / head `.` for each of:<br>`git reset --hard$(true)`<br>`` git reset --hard`true` ``<br>`git reset$(true) --hard`<br>`$(true)git reset --hard`<br>`git checkout .$(true)`<br>`git checkout -- .$(true)`<br>`git checkout$(true) .`<br>`git restore .$(true)`<br>`git restore$(true) .`<br>`git clean$(true) -fd`<br>`git branch --delete$(true) --force feat`<br>`rm$(true) -rf src`<br>BUM base rc2 / head `.` for `gh pr merge$(true) 1` and `gh pr merge$(true) 1 --repo o/r --squash`. TG still asks for these two, so only the checks gate regresses there.<br>Still refused at head: `rm -rf$(true) src`, `git clean -fdx$(true)`, `git branch -D$(true) feat`. _(HIGH)_ | Same fix as SEC-1, applied once in `_bd_words` so all three hooks get it. For example, return each word with the marker removed for option and subcommand matching, while keeping it unreadable for TG's checks. Add these rows to the block-destructive-git, block-destructive-rm and block-unchecked-merge suites. |
### P2 — Security Concerns
| **SEC-3 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1459-1460`**<br>The "`"$CMD"` is quoted" exception checks only the first character of the segment. A word that starts with a quote but then has an unquoted variable is still split into words by bash. With `CMD='gh release create v9'`, the stub showed bash running `gh release create v9` for each of these, all TG `.` at head:<br>`CMD='gh release create v9'; ""$CMD`<br>`''$CMD`<br>`"$E"$CMD`<br>`"${E}"$CMD`<br>`"$@"$CMD`<br>`CMD='gh pr merge 1'; ""$CMD` (BUM `.` too)<br>`CMD='git push --tags'; ""$CMD`<br>The plain `$CMD` form asks at head, so this rule is new in this diff and these spellings get around it. _(HIGH)_ | Skip the rule only when the whole word is one quoted span: the segment starts with a quote, the matching close quote is the last character of the word, and nothing unquoted follows. |
| **SEC-4 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1458`** and **`:1833`**<br>The "a word with a `/` names a file" exception also matches the `/` inside parameter expansions such as `${X/a/b}`, `${X//a/b}`, `${X%/}` and `${X#*/}`, which bash expands and splits like any variable.<br>`CMD='gh release create v9'; ${CMD%/}`: TG `.` (stub ran it)<br>`CMD=gh_release_create_v9; ${CMD//_/ }`: TG `.`<br>`CMD='gh pr merge 1'; ${CMD%/}`: TG `.`, BUM `.`<br>`CD=cdx; ${CD/x/} ../other && git push origin master`: TG `.`, where the `$CD` form asks. Bash ran the `cd`.<br>`E=eval; ${E%/} 'cd ../other' && git push origin master`: TG `.`; bash ran the eval. _(HIGH)_ | Look for the `/` only outside `${...}`: remove every `${...}` from the word first, then test for `*/*`. |
| **SEC-5 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1457`** (`TG_KEPT`, set at `:2028`)<br>The heredoc exception covers the whole text, not just the body lines. Once any heredoc body is kept, an unquoted `$CMD` on a real command line after it is not asked about. Each of these runs `gh release create v9` (stub confirmed), with TG `.` at head where the plain form asks:<br>`CMD="gh release create v9"` / `cat >/dev/null <<EOF` / `x` / `EOF` / `$CMD`<br>the same with `cat <<EOF >/dev/null`, `: <<EOF` or `bash <<EOF echo x EOF` before `$CMD`<br>`bash <<'EOF'` / `CMD='gh release create v9'; $CMD` / `EOF` (the body runs in a shell, so `$CMD` there is a command, not data). _(HIGH)_ | Exempt only segments that come from heredoc body lines, by tracking which segments are body lines. Do not exempt a body that is fed to a shell. |
| **SEC-6 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:2119-2120`**<br>The exception for `eval` of one assignment is meant for `eval "v=\${$name}"`, but it accepts any variable in the value, and eval runs that value as shell text.<br>`CMD=';gh release create v9'; eval "X=$CMD"`: TG `.` at base and head; the stub ran `gh release create v9`<br>`eval X=$CMD` and `CMD='...;gh pr merge 1'`: TG `.`, BUM `.`<br>The header documents only the indirect `\${$name}` form as not covered; a direct `$CMD` is the "eval of a variable" case it says asks. _(HIGH)_ | Allow only when every `$` in the evaluated word comes from an escaped `\$` in the raw text (the `${$name}` shape). Otherwise emit `cmdUnread`. |
### P3 — Security Improvements
| **SEC-7 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1153`**<br>These were allowed at base too and are not regressions; they are the same marker class as SEC-1.<br>`gh api graphql -f query$(true)='mutation{mergePullRequest(...)}'`: TG `.` at both (BUM refuses)<br>`gh api --method$(true) POST repos/o/r/releases`: TG `.` at both<br>`gh api -X$(true) POST repos/o/r/releases -f tag_name=v9`: TG `.` at both; the stub received `api -X POST repos/o/r/releases`. _(HIGH)_ | This is covered by the SEC-1 fix (judge with the marker removed); add these three to the pinned rows. |

## Code review of f3a39d72..c51e2877: tier gate and shared command parser, round 5
All seven named test files pass at c51e2877: e2e-tier-gate 2629/0, e2e-tier-gate-fences 339/0, e2e-guard-refusals 329/0, block-unchecked-merge 193/0, block-destructive-git 142/0, block-destructive-rm 65/0, block-destructive-branch 32/0.
### P1 — Critical (Blocks Merge)
### P2 — Should Fix
| **F1 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1498`, `:2109`**<br>Introduced in bb091f8a. The "a shell reads its script from its input" rule fires on a shell's *name used as an argument*, with no pipe feeding it, and asks as a Tier 3 action ("may merge a pull request or create a release"). The scan path (1498) treats any later word of an unknown program as a possible program. The command-word path (2109) does the same after `command -v`. In every case below, base gives no decision and head asks with the "shell that reads its script" reason:<br>`which bash && gh pr view 1`<br>`command -v bash && gh pr list`<br>`type bash; gh pr list`<br>`ls /bin/sh && gh pr list`<br>`file /bin/bash && gh pr list`<br>`docker run --rm img bash && gh pr list`<br>`direnv export bash && gh pr view 1`<br>`x=$(direnv export bash) && gh pr view 1`<br>`eval "$(direnv export bash)" && gh pr view 1`<br>`eval "$(starship init bash)"; gh pr list`<br>`docker compose run app sh && git push origin main`<br>With no pipe and no redirection, the shell's input is the Bash tool's own input, not text from the command, so nothing unread can run. The header's list of accepted extra prompts (around line 390) names only "a shell … after `;` rather than `\|`", not a shell name passed as an argument. _(HIGH)_ | Only ask when the segment is fed by a pipe. `_bd_segments` already knows where it split on `\|`, so have it mark pipe-fed segments, and require that mark at both 1498 and 2109. At minimum, treat `command -v`/`-V` as running nothing, and add `which`, `type`, `whereis`, `ls`, `stat`, `file`, `readlink` and `realpath` to the print-only words. Add tests: `which bash && gh pr view 1` stays silent, `direnv export bash && gh pr view 1` stays silent, and `echo x \| sudo bash` still asks. |
| **F2 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:2119`**<br>Introduced in 840f16ec. The eval exemption is broader than the header says. The header (251, 369) exempts only `eval "v=\${$name}"`, which reads a variable by name. The code exempts *any* `eval NAME=<value>` whose written value has no `$(`, backquote or substitution marker. So `eval "v=$CMD"` and `eval v=$CMD` pass while `eval "$CMD"` asks, yet eval runs whatever follows a `;` in `$CMD`. Proof: `bash -c 'eval "v=$1"' _ '1; echo INJECTED'` prints `INJECTED`. Probes, base vs head:<br>`eval "v=$CMD"; gh pr list`: none vs none<br>`eval v=$CMD; gh pr list`: none vs none<br>`eval "$CMD"; gh pr list`: none vs ask<br>No test covers this: row 78 tests only the `\${$name:-}` form. _(HIGH)_ | Exempt only the indirect-read shape. Check the segment as written (`TG_SEGTXT`, because `_bd_words` has already removed the backslash) against `NAME=\${$NAME}` or `NAME=\${$NAME:-…}`, with no other `$` in the word. Flow's own uses (address.md:815, review.md:1273/1277/1762/1796/2245, start.md:995) all have that shape. Add tests: `eval "v=$CMD"; gh pr list` and `eval v=$CMD; gh pr list` ask (cmdUnread), and row 78 stays silent. |
### P3 — Consider
| **F3 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1457-1463`**<br>The exemption for a quoted `$CMD` checks whether the *segment* starts with a quote, not whether the command word is quoted. Base vs head:<br>`X=1 "$CMD"; gh pr list`: none vs ask (an extra prompt)<br>`"$CMD"; gh pr list`: none vs none<br>`"$A"$B; gh pr list`: none vs none, although the unquoted `$B` is word-split, so `A=gh B=' pr merge 1'` runs a merge.<br>Separately, the `$CMD`-alone ask only fires when the text also contains gh, push, merge or release, because of the pre-parse filter: `$CMD` alone gives none, but `$CMD # push` asks. The header (264-267, 345) says plainly that `$CMD` asks. _(HIGH)_ | Decide whether the command word is quoted from the word itself: record a per-word flag in `_bd_words` for a word that is entirely one quoted string. Reword the header to say the `$CMD` rule applies only to text that passes the gh/push/merge/release filter. |
| **F4 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:131`, `:1666`**<br>Introduced. `git checkout -b <name> <start>` is treated as an upstream change that makes every later push ask, even one with an explicit remote and refspec: `git checkout -b feat2 origin/main && git push -u origin HEAD` gives none in base and asks in head, while `git checkout -b feat3 && git push -u origin HEAD` stays silent. A start-point checkout only writes `branch.<name>.remote/merge`, which cannot change where `git push origin HEAD` goes or what it sends. This is the branch command in `commands/start.md:556` and `skills/branch-and-task-management/SKILL.md:24`, so it costs a prompt when an agent chains the push onto it. No test covers it: rows 107-109 push with no remote, and row 127 has no start point. _(HIGH)_ | When a push names both a remote and a refspec, ignore earlier `branch.*` upstream changes: they only affect a push that names neither. Add a test that `git checkout -b x origin/main && git push -u origin HEAD` is silent. |
| **F5 · performance · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:779`**<br>The new pass that reads text piped into a shell starts on `*'\|'*[Ss][Hh]*`. Any pipe followed by "push", "sh", ".sh" or "gh"-style text meets that, and the pass then re-segments the whole command and runs `_bd_words` (one awk process per quoted segment). On a 300-line `echo '…' \| tee -a log` script ending in `git push`: block-destructive went from 1.48 s to 2.95 s, tier-gate from 9.13 s to 10.77 s. Single 20 KB arguments are unaffected (p1: 0.46 s to 0.60 s). _(HIGH)_ | Start the pass only when a shell name appears as a whole word after a `\|`, or fold the check into the first loop of `_bd_expand_interpreter_args`, which already reads each segment's words. |
| **F6 · maintainability · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:284`**<br>Pre-existing comment, now stale: "Quoting, word splitting and redirections are left to `_rm_tokenise` below." `_bd_words` is now the reader, and `_rm_tokenise` sits above this line and is only used by `s1-guard.sh:403`. The lists of shell names also disagree: `_bd_shell_reads_stdin` (line 314) has `mksh` but not `busybox`, and `_bd_is_interpreter` has `busybox` but not `mksh`. _(MEDIUM)_ | Point the comment at `_bd_words`, and use one shared list of shell names. |
| **F7 · tests · `plugins/flow/tests/e2e-tier-gate-fences.test.sh:2-4`, `:46-52`, `:71`**<br>(a) The header says "every bash fence", but the extractor matches only ```` ```bash ````. The 62 ```` ```! ```` fences, which Claude Code runs when the command loads (`references/command-output-format.md:3`), are not tested. One of them asks in both trees: `commands/merge.md` `!` fence #2, a read-only `gh api graphql -f query="query { … \"$OWNER\" … }"`, gets the "gh api … cannot be read" reason. I did not establish whether PreToolUse hooks run on `!` fences.<br>(b) Two of the asks the test lists as expected are avoidable prompts in flow's own instructions. `release.md#2` asks because `git push -q -u origin "$RELEASE_BRANCH"` is a variable refspec, even though the branch was just created with `git switch -c`. `flow-triggers-quickstart.md#3` asks on `git push -u origin feature/synthetic-pr-test` because a branch created earlier in the same text is read as "a name that does not exist yet". Both trees behave the same.<br>(c) Matching expected asks by ordinal fails loudly when a fence is inserted. My line-based extractor agreed with the regex on all 168 fences. _(HIGH)_ | (a) Either extract `!` fences too, or narrow the header to "every ```bash fence" and say why. (b) Use `git push -u origin HEAD` in release.md and in the quickstart, or have the hook treat a name made by `checkout -b`/`switch -c` earlier in the same command as a local branch. Then drop those two from the expected asks. (c) Also check that each expected-ask fence contains its action text, so a shifted ordinal cannot pass by coincidence. |
### For decision: new prompts the header already accepts (not graded as defects)
### What is clean
- **block-destructive:** every base/head difference is a fix. `rm -rf build &>/dev/null` and `rm -rf build>/dev/null` were refused and are now allowed (`build` is a safe directory), and `git reset --hard>/dev/null` was allowed and is now refused. 37 other rm and git forms are unchanged, including `rm -rf build && make`, heredoc commits, `for` loops, `trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT`, `npm run x | tee log` and `(cd sub && rm -rf build)`.
- **block-unchecked-merge:** no difference on 13 merge shapes, including `&> /dev/null`, `>& /dev/null`, glued `1>`, `bash <<<"…"` and `0<<<`.
### Summary
